video.title: The Most Overlooked $81K/Month Business Anyone Can Start

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Parker Smith, a 25-year-old former DoorDash driver who built and sold a remote cleaning business, runs a holiday lighting business, and in 85 days grew Raleigh Water Pros, a whole-home water filtration installer, to $81k in August revenue with ~$500 setup. He advertises a $2,699 installed price via static Meta ads to undercut $6-8k in-home-sales competitors, pays independent plumbers ~$500 per install, and runs ~40% gross margin with ~$175 CAC. He details speed-to-lead texting, relentless follow-up, Indeed plumber hiring, inventory management and review collection. Key takeaway: find high-ticket trade services with inflated market rates, wedge on price, and sub out the labour.

speakers.name: Parker Smith
speakers.description: 25-year-old founder of Raleigh Water Pros, holiday lighting business; sold a cleaning business; Parker Home Services on YouTube

ideas.name: Price-led whole-home water filtration with subcontracted plumbers (Raleigh Water Pros)
ideas.one_liner: Sell whole-home softener/carbon systems plus RO drinking water at a transparent $2,699 installed price via Facebook ads, undercutting $6-8k in-home-sales competitors, with independent plumbers doing installs.
ideas.business_model: Per-install project sales (~40% gross margin, ~$1,000 net target per job)
ideas.customer: Homeowners in Raleigh, NC (ads targeted 30-60 age in radius), often already quoted by Culligan/Kinetico/Leaf Home
ideas.problem: Big brands charge $6-8k via elaborate in-home sales; many are priced out
ideas.offer: Flagship 10x54 mixed-bed resin+carbon tank with RO drinking water, installed for $2,699 incl. tax; upsells (~$500)

pricing.notes: Price chosen as cheapest that still nets ~$1,000/job; raise once reputation allows. Average ticket ~$3,000-3,300 with upsells.

acquisition_channels.details: ~95% of customers from Facebook/Meta lead-form ads; static image of the unit with '$2,699 installed'; broad radius geo + age 30-60; $100-400/day spend; $30-40 per lead; ~$175 CAC.

quote.text: it was just a static image ad that was a photo of our unit and it said $26.99 installed and that was it
quote.speaker: Parker Smith

acquisition_channels.details: 52 five-star reviews in ~80 days; #1 for water filtration on east Raleigh.

ideas.delivery: Licensed independent plumbers (hired via sponsored Indeed post) install in ~4 hours for ~$400-650; inventory in a smart-lock storage unit with LTL freight; operations manager owns lead-to-install; GHL auto-texts new leads, humans call.
unit_economics_claims: $2,700 sale: ~$950 hardware, ~$100 misc, ~$500 plumber = ~40% gross margin
June ~$15k (5 installs), July ~$50k (16 jobs), August $81k (~25 jobs)
Ops manager $200 per closed job + base
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: First sale on day one of ads (June 8) with $41 of ad spend

acquisition.how: Meta ads can be run by agents with spend approval; lead-form leads in UK are opt-in so follow-up texts/calls to people who requested a quote are allowed, but closing still relies on human calls.

onboarding.how: Phone qualification and quotes by humans; automated intro text.

delivery.how: Physical installation by plumbers; inventory handling.

support.how: Plumber coordination and service issues human.

uk_applicability.notes: UK has hard-water regions (London/South East) and water softener market; needs WRAS-compliant installs and Gas Safe not required; prices in GBP; Meta ads work similarly. UK homes rarely have garages for tanks; softeners go under sinks.

risks: Thin follow-up capacity as a one-man show

tactics.name: Price-anchored ad against premium incumbents
steps: Find a service where big brands sell via in-home sales at high prices
Pick price that still nets ~$1,000/job
Run a static image ad: product photo + '$X installed'
Target broad radius, age 30-60
Raise price as reviews accumulate

quote.text: we opened up a uh a Chevy dealership next to a Ferrari dealership
quote.speaker: Parker Smith

tactics.name: Speed-to-lead text then relentless follow-up
steps: GHL auto-texts instantly: 'Hi X, this is Jack with Raleigh Water Pros, when's a good time for 5 minutes to quote?'
Wait ~1 hour, then call and text
Follow up until they buy, opt out or say leave me alone
Expect 4-8 touches before first conversation; closes up to 49 days later

quote.text: Hey, Kevin, this is Jack with Raleigh Waterpros. I got your form. When's a good time for us to chat for 5 minutes
quote.speaker: Parker Smith

tactics.name: Hire independent plumbers via sponsored Indeed post
steps: Post: licensed, own supplies, $75-125/hour, 2+ jobs/week, only softener/filtration/RO installs
$90/day for 4 days
Pick plumbers busy ~30 hrs/week who want more, not struggling or fully booked
Take them to coffee/lunch to onboard

tactics.name: Piggyback on competitors' water tests
steps: Ask every lead if they have a water test
Use competitor's test to remove knowledge gap
For city water, use EWG public database instead of in-home test
Send wells to third-party testing

tactics.name: Review maniac for high-ticket service
steps: Ask every customer for a review after the job
Offer to drop free salt later and ask spouse/brother to review too

tactics.name: Remote-access inventory storage
steps: 10x20 storage unit with smart lock
Per-plumber access codes and delivery driver code
LTL freight with same driver
Owner visits twice a month

tactics.name: Pay ops manager per closed job, not %
steps: $200 flat per closed job plus base
Owns lead-to-install end-to-end

tactics.name: Take deposits if no inventory
steps: Collect deposit at signing if ordering after sale
Prevents customers walking during delays

warnings.warning: Running out of inventory halted installs for a week; hold stock.

quote.text: that 81 grand that we did was with zero installs in the second week of August. H because we didn't have product
quote.speaker: Parker Smith

warnings.warning: A one-person operation can't follow up with all leads; CAC rises when leads go cold.
About 10% of Meta lead-form leads deny filling the form.
Don't hire struggling or fully booked subcontractors.
Don't judge sales/marketing data until at least a month in.
Don't sell as an outsider without enough technical knowledge to talk to tradespeople.

quote.text: your business lives or dies on the plumbers
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: UK: follow-up texts are fine to people who requested a quote, but buying or cold-texting lists of homeowners breaks PECR.

lessons.lesson: Your margin is my opportunity: many trade services have made-up market rates.

quote.text: the going rate for this service was $8,000 has nothing to do with water filtration
quote.speaker: Parker Smith

lessons.lesson: Putting the price in the ad replaces a skilled salesperson by filtering for educated buyers.
Pick the cheapest price that still hits your target net per job, then raise with reputation.
The model (sub out installs, own marketing) matters more than the product.
Most high-ticket sales close after multiple touches; quitting early wastes leads.

quote.text: 17 of them were closed at least one additional touch point
quote.speaker: Parker Smith

lessons.lesson: Hire one owner for the whole lead-to-job pipeline rather than a pure salesperson.
The higher the ticket, the harder you must push for reviews.
Blue-collar niches are overlooked because people think margins are only in tech.
Prior businesses teach delegation: stop being the means of production.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with detailed, mostly consistent unit economics and funnel numbers; early stage (85 days).
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Parker sells home service coaching; Chris sells $19 business plans/$5 community; Beehiiv sponsor.
